issues.legal_issue: The reasonableness of compound interest on a mortgage loan must be assessed by reference to the circumstances and risks apparent when the loan was made, and excessive interest may be reduced.
material_facts: The lender advanced money under mortgages at 15 per cent compound interest with quarterly rests.
The debtor was already in debt, and the principal property offered as security was dilapidated; there was also a threatened challenge to her title.
The security was not markedly inadequate, and the threat of a further suit was not regarded as serious; the lender advanced more money on the same interest terms even after that suit was filed.
The High Court reduced the interest to 10 per cent compound interest with yearly rests, and the Supreme Court upheld that assessment.
issues.conclusion: The High Court correctly reduced the contractual interest to 10 per cent compound interest with yearly rests; the reduction was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Usurious Loans (Madras Amendment) Act, 1937 empowers a court to grant relief where a transaction was substantially unfair. Excessive interest gives rise to a rebuttable presumption of substantial unfairness. Whether interest is excessive is assessed by looking back to the date of the loan and considering the risk apparent to the creditor, the presence and value of security, the debtor’s financial condition and known prior transactions, other circumstances affecting the parties, and whether compound interest was charged and how frequently it was added to principal. No rate is excessive independently of the circumstances. The Court relied on Venkatarao v. Venkatratnam, A.I.R. 1952 Madras 872, and Sri Balasaraswati v. A. Parameswara Aiyar, A.I.R. 1957 Madras 122.

rule.if: mortgage_interest_appeal and security_not_markedly_inadequate and title_challenge_not_serious and lender_advanced_further_money_on_same_terms

predicates.mortgage_interest_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the rate of interest payable under mortgage loans.
predicates.security_not_markedly_inadequate: The property offered as security was not markedly inadequate in relation to the loans.
predicates.title_challenge_not_serious: A threatened challenge to the debtor’s title was not regarded as a serious repayment risk.
predicates.lender_advanced_further_money_on_same_te: The lender advanced additional money on the same interest terms despite the threatened title challenge.

issues.definition: When a mortgage-interest appeal concerns security that was not markedly inadequate, a title challenge that was not serious, and further advances on unchanged terms, the contractual interest is scaled down.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not disturb a discretionary reduction of interest applicable after a suit is filed when the circumstances support leaving that reduction in place.
material_facts: The High Court reduced the interest rate from the filing of the suit, exercising its discretion over interest for the period while the suit was pending.
The mortgages had been made many years before the suit was filed, and the creditor would receive interest substantially exceeding the principal amount of the loans.
The Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with the High Court’s reduction, although the High Court had not stated its reasons.
issues.conclusion: The reduction of interest for the period after the suit was filed was left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The court may exercise discretion over interest for the period while a suit is pending. The Supreme Court found no basis to interfere with that exercise of discretion in the circumstances, including the substantial delay before suit and the substantial interest the creditor would receive. No earlier case was cited for this point.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_pendente_lite_interest and lower_court_exercised_interest_discretion and suit_filed_long_after_loan and expected_interest_substantially_exceeds_principal

predicates.appeal_challenging_pendente_lite_interes: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the interest set for the period while a suit was pending.
predicates.lower_court_exercised_interest_discretio: The lower court exercised its discretion in setting interest for the period after the suit was filed.
predicates.suit_filed_long_after_loan: The suit was filed long after the loan was made.
predicates.expected_interest_substantially_exceeds_: The creditor would receive interest substantially exceeding the principal amount of the loan.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a lower court’s discretionary award of interest after suit filing, and the suit was delayed and expected interest substantially exceeds principal, the appellate court leaves the reduction undisturbed.
